requirements.text: * A builder mindset. You own projects end to end, think carefully about data models, performance, and maintainability, and have taken prototypes to production with a clear sense of the reliability and scale tradeoffs.

* 3–5+ years building backend systems, ideally real-time, stateful, or event-driven workloads, with strong distributed systems fundamentals: message queues (Kafka, Pulsar), distributed locks, pub/sub, and their failure modes.
* Experience building infrastructure for LLMs in production: tool calling, streaming, token budgets, or evaluation harnesses, and a sense of what agents need from the systems beneath them.

* Experience designing data models for messy, interconnected domains. You know how to structure data so it stays correct as it grows and changes, and you think about how it will be queried and served before you write the schema. You’ve made schema and storage decisions that held up under scale, and you know the cost of getting them wrong.
* You keep work moving. You balance speed of execution with code quality, unblock yourself when you can, and pull in the right people at the right time when you can’t.
* Hands-on with vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Turbopuffer) or hybrid search systems
* Experience with Kotlin/JVM (our primary stack) or Rust, MongoDB, Postgres, or Redis, and WebSockets or other real-time patterns
* You’ve built sandboxing or isolation systems with containers or microVMs (e.g., Firecracker, gVisor), or managed fleets across heterogeneous machines
* You’ve worked on filesystem layers such as FUSE, overlay filesystems, or remote-backed storage
* You’ve worked with event sourcing, lineage, or provenance data, where the record of what happened is itself a product
